transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Leo (Redwood SE), Marta (Silvernest HoD), Omar (Silvernest ML Eng), Claire (CTO), Ravi (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Silvernest is a regulated fintech exploring an open-model POC to extract structured fields from customer emails and perform multilingual entity normalization. Primary success metrics are 95% extraction F1 on core dataset, tail latency < 450ms p95 on average request (<= 2k tokens), and cost target < $0.01 per processed request. They prefer EU data residency and need KMS integration for keys. Discussed model shortlist (smaller 8–13B vs larger 40–70B), quantized variants, batch sizing, and a 3-week bench + 2-week pilot timeline. Redwood to provide bench harness, cost estimates, and a proposed Dedicated configuration.

Topics covered:
- Scope & success criteria
- Workload sizing and token distribution
- Model shortlist and quality tradeoffs (multilingual + financial domain)
- Benchmark plan, metrics, tooling, and timeline
- Security, residency, and KMS questions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jared from Redwood, with Priya and Leo on the call. can you each do a quick intro?
[00:13] Marta: hi Marta here, head of data at Silvernest. we run customer support and claims triage, lots of incoming emails, some in french and spanish.
[00:27] Claire: Claire, CTO. looking at how we can automate extraction and canonicalize merchant names, amounts, and dispute reason.
[00:34] Omar: Omar, ML engineer; i'm the one who will run the bench with redwood. we have a small internal cluster but want to evaluate the open model route before building infra.
[00:40] Ravi: ravi from compliance. we need to make sure data residency and KMS fit our policy, also audit logs.
[00:48] Priya: great, thanks. quick agenda: confirm success criteria, go through size of workload, propose model shortlist and bench plan, then timeline. sound good?
[00:55] Omar: yes

[01:05] Jared: first, can you walk us through success criteria — what counts as a win for Silvernest?
[01:12] Marta: primary is extraction accuracy, we measure F1 over the labeled fields — merchant, amt, date, dispute_code. target is 95% on the core 80% slice and acceptable degradation +-5% for tail. second is latency — we need p95 below about 450ms because this impacts our chatflows. third is cost — under $0.01 per request target at scale.
[01:34] Claire: timeline wise we want something we can trial in production in 8 weeks if POC looks good.

[01:42] Priya: good — those are clear. on workload sizing, Omar, can you summarize traffic patterns? token sizes per request? qps?
[01:50] Omar: typical email body averages 600 tokens, but our pipeline truncates to 2k for long threads. concurrent requests spike around 100 qps during business hours for the EU cluster, steady-state ~20 qps. monthly volume about 25M processed messages.
[02:10] Priya: ok so bench should mimic 20 qps steady and a 100 qps 5-minute spike. also include 2k token tail samples. we'll capture latency distribution with and without batching.

[02:28] Leo: quick note on KV cache, sorry i said KV cash earlier in infra doc — we meant KV cache for prefix cache to accelerate repeated customer queries. that will help cost and latency for conversational followups.

[02:40] Omar: that cache will be big — we have a lot of recurring entities across customers.

[02:47] Jared: model shortlist — we propose starting with 1) Mistral-x-7B (quantized 4-bit), 2) Falcon-40B-instruct (qat or int8), 3) Llama-3-70B-open variant (bigger baseline), and 4) a smaller multilingual specialist like NLLB-ish adaptation or OpenL3 13B variant. Any thoughts?
[03:10] Marta: are these all publicly available? we prefer open-source to avoid API lock-in.
[03:14] Priya: yes, all viable open variants; we will provide both hosted and Dedicated configs so you can see tradeoffs.
[03:20] Claire: question — the 40b vs 7b, do we expect a big quality gap on financial jargon and multilingual french/spanish?
[03:28] Priya: generally larger models do better on edge cases and low-resource languages, but quantization and instruction tuning matter a lot. for structured extraction, sometimes a well-tuned 13B with domain examples can match a 40B, especially if you do retrieval/shot prompting or light finetune. for French/Spanish, models trained on diverse corpora (Mistral, Llama) tend to be ok.
[03:50] Omar: finetune is not an option for us initially due to data residency, but we can do few-shot and retrieval.

[03:58] Jared: benchmark plan — we'll run these models across 3 axes: quality (F1 on labeled set), latency (cold vs warmed, p50/p95/p99), and cost per 1000 requests. Priya will set up a harness that runs the 20 qps steady load and a 100 qps spike; also run multilingual slices (EN/FR/ES).
[04:20] Priya: for tooling we'll use Redwood's bench harness which records token counts, GPU utilization, batching efficiency, and also calculate cost estimates using reserved Dedicated pricing vs hosted unit cost. we'll provide a shared spreadsheet with results.

[04:36] Omar: what's the expected throughput on a Dedicated 8xA100 pool for the 7b vs 40b?
[04:41] Priya: rough ballpark: quantized 7b can do 2-3k rps per GPU with batching but depends on latency targets; a 40b might do 200–400 rps per GPU. those are very rough — bench will measure real numbers with your token distribution.

[04:59] Marta: cost math is important. show us end-to-end (per request) including overheads. we have our own cost model, so aligning metrics will help.

[05:10] Ravi: security checklist — do you support customer-managed KMS? SSO? audit logs? can Redwood Dedicated be deployed in our EU VPC?
[05:20] Priya: yes on Dedicated we can integrate KMS (bring-your-own keys), SAML SSO, role-based access, and audit logs. Private deployments are possible if needed for air-gapped. for EU residency we can pin regions to eu-west.
[05:34] Claire: any pen test / compliance docs we can review?
[05:36] Jared: we'll send SOC2 Type II and our security whitepaper, plus a short KMS integration doc.

[05:45] Omar: benchmark metrics — for quality eval what datasets will you expect? we will send our labeled sample but do you recommend augmenting with synthetic edge cases?
[05:54] Priya: yes, send your 500 core samples and we'll add 200 synthetic tail cases (multilang & obfuscated merchant names). that helps stress rare patterns.

[06:05] Leo: on evaluation, we'll compute per-field F1, macro F1 across languages, and a confidence calibration metric. also tie-in a human review pass rate — e.g., how often human-in-the-loop needs to correct.

[06:18] Marta: for success we want F1 >= 0.95 on core and human correction under 7% in production.

[06:25] Jared: timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) – align on samples and bench plan. Week 1 – Redwood sets up bench and runs smoke tests. Week 2 – full bench across models and slices. Week 3 – analyze, select candidate model(s). Week 4–5 – pilot deploy on Dedicated (config, KMS, small prod traffic) and run end-to-end validation. so roughly 5 weeks end-to-end; customer said earlier they'd like 8 weeks to be safe.

[06:50] Claire: that fits our internal change windows. we need decision gates though — after bench we have a go/no-go based on quality and cost.

[06:57] Ravi: small note on logs — we cannot store raw PII outside eu region; please redact or pseudonymize in bench samples.
[07:05] Priya: absolutely — please anonymize PII before upload; we'll also sign an NDA for the dataset if you prefer.

[07:12] Omar: question about quantization quality — do you have example shifts we should expect when moving to 4-bit int?
[07:19] Leo: yes, we typically see small drops in exact token generation for some models but for structured extraction the impact is often modest if using task-specific prompt templates; bench will quantify any delta.

[07:30] Marta: is it possible to test a nearest-neighbor retrieval augmentation (RAG) for merchant normalization?
[07:36] Priya: yes, we can include a retrieval baseline — Redwood Optimize recommends a retrieval + small model combo to reduce cost and improve canonicalization. we'll show a caching strategy and retrieval latency contribution.

[07:50] Omar: for the bench harness, what outputs do you give us? raw transcripts, per-request logs?
[07:56] Priya: we provide per-request CSV (non-PII), aggregate dashboards (latency, cost), and a bench spreadsheet with comparisons. also GC logs and config used.

[08:05] Jared: OK to recap next steps?
[08:08] Marta: yes please
[08:10] Jared: Redwood will: 1) send benchmark spreadsheet and test harness + instructions (Jared/Priya) — due 2027-06-17, 2) propose Dedicated sizing options and cost estimates — due 2027-06-17, 3) run smoke tests on our side once you upload the sample set. Customer will: 1) anonymize and upload 500 sample requests + label set — Omar to do by 2027-06-18, 2) confirm compliance contacts for KMS & legal.
[08:36] Claire: we'll block time for the pilot kickoff next Tuesday, internal invite after we get the spreadsheet.

[08:45] Ravi: one last compliance ask — do you support HSM-backed keys?
[08:50] Priya: yes, Redwood Dedicated can integrate with HSM or cloud KMS providers; we'll include the HSM note in the security doc.

[08:58] Jared: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with docs and next steps.
[09:03] Marta: thanks, talk soon.

END OF TRANSCRIPT

- POC type: open-model evaluation -> shortlist across 7B/13B/40B/70B candidates; include quantized variants and a retrieval-augmented baseline.
- Success criteria: field extraction F1 >= 0.95 (core), p95 latency <= 450ms, cost target < $0.01/request, human correction <7%.
- Bench scope: steady 20 qps + 100 qps spike, 2k token tail, EN/FR/ES slices, per-field F1 and calibration metrics.
- Timeline: bench (1–2 weeks), pilot Dedicated conf (weeks 3–4), production decision by week 6–8.
